reading.body:
Delaware's 2025, 2026 legislative session treats data centers and large energy users as a distinct regulatory category, with four bills filed on those subjects in the span of about six weeks.

SB312 amends three titles of state code to address data centers directly. HB233 addresses large energy use facilities under Title 26, the title that governs utilities. SB353 proposes a moratorium on data center development. HB450 rewrites land use across four titles. Read together, these are the pieces of a siting fight: where compute gets built, who supplies its power, and whether the state pauses new construction while it decides. That is the compute-buildings-power chain showing up as statutory language rather than as an industry talking point.

The AI-specific bills sit in a different register. HJR7 directs the Artificial Intelligence Commission to build a regulatory sandbox for agentic AI. HB16 amends the code relating to that commission. HB404 creates an AI and extended reality pilot in schools. HB191 concerns medical professionals, titles, and nonhuman entities. None of these touch compute supply. The state is regulating what AI does and who may deploy it, while separately debating whether the physical infrastructure behind it can keep being built.

The data does not show outcomes. A bill's presence here means it was filed or acted on by the listed date, not that it passed, and the list mixes appropriations bills, interstate compacts for athletic trainers and massage therapists, and stablecoin law alongside the AI and data center items. It also does not show how much load Delaware data centers actually draw, what the moratorium would cover, or whether the energy and land use bills were drafted in response to specific projects. Those are the questions the titles raise and the record does not answer.
